newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Telkom says no action against partners.
newsitem.headline: Telkom says no action against partners.

text.p: Indonesia's state-controlled telecommunications giant PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia (Telkom) said on Tuesday it did not deem it necessary to fine its partners for failing to meet telephone line installation targets in 1996.

Indonesian parliament members said on Monday that three of Telkom's five joint operating scheme partners should be fined for failing to reach their 1996 targets for the construction of new telephone lines, Bisnis Indonesia newspaper reported on Tuesday.

"The deadline for all five to meet the target of installing some two million lines is March 1999. I don't think it necessary to fine them now for failing to reach last year's target," director Harry Supangkat told Reuters.
"Some of them may lag behind in terms of the number of telephone installations last year as it was the starting year when things could not be that easy. They may catch up this year," Supangkat said.

Bisnis Indonesia reported that consortiums Daya Mitra Malindo and Mitra Global Telekomunikasi Indonesia had not installed any telephone lines in 1996. Bukaka Singtel International installed only 20,000 lines against a 1996 target of 34,700 lines, it said.
